Both the accused are facing trial for offences u/s 356/379/411/34 IPC.

The genesis of the prosecution story is that on 13.07.2021 at about 09:00 pm at DDU Marg, Near Rouse Avenue School, Delhi, both accused used criminal force on complainant Sh. Anil Mehto and snatched his mobile phone.
The criminal law was set into motion pursuant to the registration of present case FIR and the investigation into the same began.
After completion of same, the charge-sheet was filed for trial of both accused for the alleged offences.

2. Thereafter, the cognizance of the offences was taken by the Court and on the basis of material available on record, charges for offences u/s 356/379/411/34 IPC were framed against both accused persons.
Both accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

sentences.text: 3. In order to establish guilt of both accused, the prosecution has examined one witnesses in all.

The accused also admitted factum of preparation of FIR bearing no. DD No- 2A dated 14.07.2021, PS IP Estate Ex. A-1, FIR No. 177/21, PS IP Estate Ex. A-2, its certificate U/s 65B Evidence Act Ex. A-3,
Endorsement on rukka vide DD no- 9A Ex. A-4, relevant entry of register no. 19 Ex. A5, Tax invoice of mobile phone Ex. A6 u/s 294 Cr.P.C.
After prosecution evidence, the statement of both accused u/s 281 Cr.PC r/w 313 Cr.P.C was recorded wherein all the incriminating circumstances were put to them.
Both accused did not lead any evidence in their defence.

4. Ld. APP for State has contended that the prosecution has established the guilt of accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts with the help of coherent testimonies of the prosecution witnesses,
therefore, both accused deserves to be convicted for the alleged offences.

5. Per contra, both Ld. Counsels for both accused have contended that both accused have been falsely implicated in the present case by the complainant and police agency have acted in connivance with the complainant.

It is also contended that the prosecution has also failed to establish the identity of both accused persons as the same person who had snatched the articles of the complainant and hence, the accused deserves to be acquitted for the alleged offences.
6.
Prior to delving into the merits of contentions advanced on behalf of parties, let us briefly discuss the testimonies of the material witnesses in brief.

6.1 PW-1 is Sh. Anil Mehto who deposed that on that day, he was driver by profession and drive taxi no. DL 1RTA 5898 and he was going to New Delhi Railway Station in his said taxi and at about 09:40 pm he was present at DDU Marg behind Rouse Avenue School and he was having his mobile phone make Redmi-8 Note Pro in his hand and the sim no. 7011363598 was activated in the mobile phone at that time and two persons came on a scooty and snatched his mobile phone and they fled away alongwith his mobile phone and he could not note the number of scooty and also could not see their faces as they were wearing helmets covering their faces and someone informed police and police had come and had taken him to police station where his report was lodged and he left police station and went to his house and on next day morning he was called by the police in police station and he reached at police station where police shown his mobile phone and two persons who were lodged in lock-up stating that they snatched his mobile phone and recovered from their possession but he had not known them.

He further deposed that police obtained his signatures on several papers which he signed at the instance of police without going through the same and he had not known the accused persons present in the court today and he had got released his mobile phone on superdari and his mobile phone had been clasped and he could not produced it.
The witness was cross-examined by Ld. APP for the State.
The witness was not cross-examined by Ld. Defence counsels.

7. Since, complainant resiled from his earlier testimony and failed to identify both the accused persons in the Court and did not depose anything in favour of prosecution, the examination of remaining formal witnesses was dispensed with.
There was no other public witness cited in the list of witnesses.
No purpose would have been served by examining the formal witnesses.

Hence, SA was State vs Azim on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187331765/
2 dispensed with and final arguments were heard.
8.

sentences.text: I have carefully gone through the record and evidence.
Perusal of case records show that PW-1/Complainant Sh. Anil Mehto is the sole eyewitness of the alleged offences.

In his testimony,
he deposed that the two boys came and snatched his mobile phone.

However, he could not identify accused persons to the fact as to whether they are the actual persons who committed the act of removing his mobile phone, it shows that he did not support his allegations against the accused persons and he did not even identify the accused persons by recognizing them as culprits, as such there is nothing on record to associate the accused persons with alleged incident or their identity and as such nothing incriminating against the accused persons could be elicited from the testimony of this witness.
He denied seeing the accused persons actually committing the alleged offences.
This witness is a sole cited eyewitness of the incident.

The remaining PWs are formal in nature as they only associated in the investigation but not are eyewitness of the incident and they have not deposed any word regarding the commission of alleged offences.
9. In absence of any incriminating evidence given by PW-1/Complainant Sh. Anil Mehto, the prosecution can never hope to prove the allegations levelled against the accused persons.
The occurrence of incident accordingly stands not proved by the prosecution.
The testimony of the other prosecution witnesses even if taken together would not be sufficient to bring home the guilt of accused persons for the alleged offences.
10. The right to speedy trial is a constitutionally guaranteed fundamental right of the accused.

The present case pertains to FIR dated 14.07.2021 and continuing the trial any further, when it is clear that prosecution can never hope to prove its case against the accused, would tantamount to violation right to speedy trial of the accused.

It has been held in P.Ram Chandra Rao Vs. State of Karnataka AIR 2002 SC 1856 that the courts should exercise its powers available under criminal procedure code to give effect to the right to speedy trial of the accused.

entities.text: P.Ram Chandra Rao Vs. State of Karnataka AIR 2002 SC 1856
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similar observations were made in Pankaj Kumar Vs. State of Maharashtra AIR 2008 SC 3057.
11.

entities.text: Pankaj Kumar Vs. State of Maharashtra AIR 2008 SC 3057
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, in Satish Mehra Vs. Delhi Administration &Anr. 1996 SCC 507 , Hon'ble Supreme Court held that valuable time of courts should not be wasted merely for formal completion of procedure,
when there is no chance of the trial culminating in conviction.

entities.text: Satish Mehra Vs. Delhi Administration &Anr. 1996 SCC 507
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Furthermore, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. S.L. Goswami Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 1972 SCC (CRI.) 258 that the accused is entitled to benefit of doubts where the onus of proving ingredients of the offences is not discharged by the prosecution.

entities.text: Dr. S.L. Goswami Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 1972 SCC (CRI.) 258
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case,
as already noted above, the prosecution has failed to discharge the onus of proving the ingredients of the offences, thus, the accused is entitled to benefit of doubts.

13. In view of the discussion made above, this Court is of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to establish beyond all reasonable doubts that on the given date, time and place accused persons Azim and Aman @ Ammu used criminal force upon the complainant Sh. Anil Mehto and snatched his mobile phone, therefore, the accused persons stands acquitted for offence u/s 356/379/41134 IPC.
